text: You get to decide what people see. That is the real difference between a public utility and a private gatekeeper. The whole point of the system you are trying to protect was to keep such decisions out of the hands of a single company. Once a carrier can pick which services to favor, the rest of the network ceases to be a common carrier in any meaningful sense. It is hard to see how innovation of the sort you want to see would survive that sort of control. That is what you are fighting for here and the rest of the plan hangs on it.
reasoning: We are at the part where the author says the bad thing is charging different services different rates. The natural next step is to say this is a form of prior restraint or that it lets a private gatekeeper pick the winners. You can mention that this kills the sort of unexpected innovation the whole system was supposed to encourage. If a company can be denied a fair price, the only thing left to decide is what it is that they are going to be allowed to offer. This is the sort of control that public utilities were never given and the distinction is worth preserving. The whole thing depends on keeping the network open to the people who use it. That is all there is to it.
